summary: Kobun Chino Otogawa (1938–2002) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Komazawa University. He taught Reginald A. Ray.
Kodo Akino (1858–1934) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University and later served as its president (学長).
Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He later taught there as a professor (attested 1978; until 2003).

Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1935–1963) and taught Kosho Uchiyama, Sodo Yokoyama, and Gudo Wafu Nishijima.
Kodo Yamada (1867–1939) was a Buddhist studies scholar. During his career, he taught at both Komazawa University and Keio University.
Koen Wellens specializes in sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under Per Kvaerne.
Koenraad Elst (born 1959) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed an MA at KU Leuven and studied at Banaras Hindu University around 1988 to 1992.

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) studied Indology and Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928, DLitt) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He held posts at Komazawa University, Keio University, and the University of Tokyo (professor 1959–1962).

Kogi Kudara (1945–2004) worked in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979, 1997) and editor for the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono (born 1944) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyushu University (PhD) and the University of Bonn, and held posts at The International University of Kagoshima (professor, attested 1991–2000) and Kyushu University (attested 1995).

Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He was a professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004) and later held positions at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004) and Yale University (~2004).

Koichi Takahashi (born 1968) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo (-2004) under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saito, and held posts there as an assistant (attested 2005) and project researcher (attested 2015).

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1973), learning under Akira Hirakawa and traditional teacher Gyoin Hashimoto. He served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1974–2005).

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) studied Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics at Kyoto University (~1957–1961) under Yutaka Ochihara. He held academic posts at Kyoto Sangyo University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (assistant professor, attested 1979).

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University (~1953–1957). He later served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1969–1978) and professor (~1978–2005).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. After studying at Waseda University (~1918–1923), he held a post there (~1944–1969) and later served as president of Taisho University (~1968–1972).
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) studied Buddhist studies and sinology at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He spent his career at Rissho University as an assistant professor (~1971–1977), department chair (~1977–2001), and director and professor (attested 2000).

Koken Unno (born 1936), a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned his doctorate at Nagoya University (-2000). He held posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University (professor, attested 2002).
